display.title: Chai Elul: The Birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe, and Yours
display.summary_short: Chai Elul is the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe. Uncle Yossi explains what a birthday means and why to know your Hebrew birthday.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, the week of Chai Elul. Uncle Yossi explains that the eighteenth of Elul is the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov, born in 1698, and of the Alter Rebbe, author of the Tanya and the Shulchan Aruch, born on the same day in 1745. On a birthday a person's mazal is strong, giving extra strength for Torah and mitzvos, so it should not slip by unnoticed. It is a day to take stock of the past year, remember the good and resolve not to repeat mistakes. A birthday is the day Hashem chose to send your neshamah down from Gan Eden into a body, so that through Torah and mitzvos it can return to an even higher level. That is why it matters to know your Hebrew birthday, and Tzivos Hashem offers to look it up for its members.
display.lesson: Your birthday is the day Hashem sent your neshamah into the world; use it to take stock and grow in Torah and mitzvos.

date.note: 'This coming Shabbos is Chai Elul' and '292 years' since 1698: Elul 5750; Tuesday 14 Elul (episode 443).
